clue.text: I'm up and coming in positive tribulation

indicators.note: in this down-style instruction, up means the letters of I'm are read from the end back to the start

parts.note: taken as written, minus the apostrophe

indicators.note: in tells us the word for coming sits inside the word for positive

parts.note: positive means sure, certain
Advent is the coming or arrival, especially of Christ

explanation.surface: Someone cheerfully on the rise despite going through hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming' looks like an adjective beside 'up and', but it is Advent, the season of the coming; 'up' turns I'M back to front, and 'in' places the coming inside the word for positive.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap or piece of bad luck is a tribulation, an ordeal that goes wrong.

clue.text: Plant one on one with six noughts

parts.note: a plant is a factory or works, a mill
the Roman numeral for one is I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener plants seedlings one beside another, with some odd talk of zeros.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb or a garden plant; here it is an industrial plant, a MILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Written as a figure, a thousand thousand is a 1 followed by six zeros.

clue.text: The object of cheese throwing

parts.note: in the pub game of ... the heavy wooden disc hurled at the pins is called a cheese, so its target is a pin

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rural cheese-rolling contest; in old English skittles the thrown disc is called a cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: In table skittles the cheese is thrown to knock down the pins, so each pin is its target.

clue.text: Portrays heartless dime novel writers

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters of dime are cut away, leaving only its outside pair

parts.note: scribes are writers, here of novels

explanation.surface: Cheap pulp-fiction authors depict their characters without much heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dime novel' reads as one phrase, cheap American fiction, but 'dime' belongs with 'heartless' and 'novel' goes with 'writers'.
explanation.definitionFit: To describe something is to depict or represent it in words.

clue.text: Hesitation takes time to be keen

indicators.note: takes means the hesitation word holds the time word inside it

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone hesitant takes a while before showing enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hesitation' is the crossword's usual spoken 'er'; 'takes' means it swallows the word for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Being eager means being enthusiastic and impatient to do something.

clue.text: Toss around and sit about south African thugs

indicators.note: around tells us the letters of toss are thrown about into a new order
about adds the letters of sit to the same scrambled pool

explanation.surface: Gangsters in South Africa throw things around and loiter idly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface splits into two separate actions, but 'around' and 'about' both signal one shuffle of all seven letters from Toss and sit; tsotsi is South African township slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsotsi is the South African township word for a young gangster or hoodlum.

clue.text: Charity event occasion for syncopated music

parts.note: a rag is a British student fund-raising event for charity
an occasion is a time, as in 'that time we met'

explanation.surface: A fund-raising evening is the right moment for some jazzy tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: A RAG is a British student charity week or event, with stunts and collections.
explanation.definitionFit: The early jazz-age piano style of Scott Joplin is built on syncopated rhythms.

clue.text: A divan factory may come up roses

definitions.text: A divan factory may come up roses

parts.words: A divan factory may come up roses
parts.note: a factory making divans is a plant producing bedding, while roses coming up in a flower bed are garden flowers set out in beds

explanation.walkthrough: Two readings: a works making beds and sheets, and a flower raised for planting out in a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant set out in a garden bed for display, and humorously a factory turning out mattresses.

clue.text: Eric ends with den's cakes

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a lair is a den; with the possessive it gives lair's

explanation.surface: Eric finishes up with his friend's pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes E and C, the first and last letters of Eric.
explanation.definitionFit: These are long cream-filled choux pastries topped with chocolate, a kind of cake.

clue.text: Rural poem "George" details Icelandic extremists

indicators.note: read as de-tails, it means the final letter of George is cut off
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: George describes some radical Icelanders in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'details' reads as de-tails: GEORGE loses its last letter to give GEORG. 'extremists' takes I and C from Icelandic.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil's Georgics are poems on farming, so the word names any poem about country life.

clue.text: Modern twist in passing

parts.note: to twist someone is to cheat or swindle them, to con them
passing means fleeting, not lasting

explanation.surface: A modern version of the novel with a twist that soon fades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' is British slang for cheat, so it gives CON.
explanation.definitionFit: Something contemporary belongs to the present day, current and up to date.

clue.text: Gather the queen gets a smack

parts.note: snow or sand that gathers into a heap forms a drift
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: A queen is slapped while people gather round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smack' looks like a slap, but it is a small fishing boat. ER is a crossword abbreviation for Queen (Elizabeth Regina).
explanation.definitionFit: Both are fishing boats: a smack is a small sailing vessel, and a drifter fishes with drift nets.

clue.text: Two guys who might be found in Moscow

definitions.text: who might be found in Moscow

parts.note: Russ is a man's name
Ian is a second man's name

explanation.surface: A pair of men who could be spotted in the Russian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The two guys are the boys' names Russ and Ian.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Russia, such as a citizen of its capital city.

clue.text: Degree of green once in a while

indicators.note: a degree of something is a portion of it, so the answer is a part of the words green once

explanation.surface: How green a lawn looks varies from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'greeN ONCE'. 'For the nonce' means for the present while.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonce means the present occasion or time being, as in the phrase for the nonce.

clue.text: It is responsible for a bust up

definitions.text: It is responsible for a bust up

parts.words: It is responsible for a bust up
parts.note: read as holding a bust up, it describes a supportive undergarment, not a cause of a quarrel

explanation.walkthrough: 'bust up' looks like a row or fight; here it is a chest that is kept lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's undergarment supporting the breasts, holding the bust up.

clue.text: Renouncer over angora bet

indicators.note: over means the letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone giving up gambling after a wager on angora wool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' signals the anagram of ANGORA BET.
explanation.definitionFit: To abnegate is to renounce or deny oneself something, so this is someone who does that.

clue.text: Mixed responses but continues forward

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of responses are jumbled up

explanation.surface: Despite a mixed reaction, someone keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' signals the anagram of RESPONSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To press on is to carry on resolutely and keep advancing.

clue.text: Gospel the preacher lost first

indicators.note: lost means the letters for first are removed from the word for the preacher

parts.note: an evangelist is a preacher of the gospel
first is written 1ST, which looks like IST

explanation.surface: The preacher lost the gospel at the very start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' written as 1ST passes for IST; 'lost' removes it from EVANGELIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangel is an old word for the gospel, the good news of Christianity.

clue.text: Serious pause at what's in the chest

parts.note: stern means grave or serious
um is the sound of a pause in speech

explanation.surface: A grave pause over what is kept in a treasure chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest' suggests a box; it is the body's chest.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone lies in the middle of the chest, where the ribs join it.

clue.text: Sharpen up the ports

indicators.note: up here means the letters of ports are turned and read backwards

explanation.surface: Smarten up the harbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PORTS back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To strop a razor is to hone its edge on a leather strap.

clue.text: Argue and fight over a bird

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the arguing word sits above the fighting word

parts.note: to spar is to argue, trade blows verbally
a row is a fight or quarrel

explanation.surface: Two people quarrel and scrap over a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts SPAR above ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: The house sparrow is a familiar small brown bird.

clue.text: More spacious area that is altogether final

parts.note: room means space or area
i.e. is short for id est, that is

indicators.note: final means only the last letter of altogether is taken

explanation.surface: A bigger space that is completely the last word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altogether final' gives R, the last letter of altogether.
explanation.definitionFit: Having more room inside means being larger and more spacious.

clue.text: Non-professional start of a man at the equalities union rally

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A man begins an equalities rally by the union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' picks the first letters of A MAN AT THE EQUALITIES UNION RALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does an activity for pleasure rather than pay is not a professional.

clue.text: Break takes time finally to readjust

indicators.note: takes means the word for break holds another letter inside it

parts.note: a rest is a break

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of time

explanation.surface: Having a break finally gives time to get yourself in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time finally' gives E, and 'takes' puts it inside REST.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset something is to set it again or adjust it anew.

clue.text: Force to hit our beauty

parts.note: g is the symbol for g-force, the acceleration of gravity
to lam is to thrash or hit
taken as written

explanation.surface: Forced to hit at our good looks.
explanation.walkthrough: G stands for gravity or g-force; LAM is slang for hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is alluring beauty or charm.

clue.text: Child's game finishes with left over pieces

parts.note: tag is a chasing game played by children
ends means finishes

explanation.surface: A child's game ends with scraps left lying about.
explanation.walkthrough: TAG is the playground chasing game.
explanation.definitionFit: Tag ends are scraps or remnants, the final bits remaining.

clue.text: A dog register

definitions.meaning: a small breed of dog bred for hunting burrowing animals
a legal register of landed property, listing estates and boundaries

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is uncommon: a land register or inventory kept by a church or manor.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a breed of small hunting hound; the other an inventory of land holdings.

clue.text: Weapon used in heated dispute?

parts.note: a weapon that hurls fire, used literally in a heated fight, with a hint of flaming words in a quarrel

explanation.walkthrough: 'heated dispute' reads as a hot-tempered row; here the heat is real flame.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that projects burning fuel, a weapon used in battle.
